analyst_view.overall: Eighth-placed Stuttgart (13 points) host seventh-placed Frankfurt (15) on Saturday evening in the race for the European places. Stuttgart lost 0-2 at Inter on Wednesday with only one shot on target, after a 0-0 at Schalke where Undav and Hoeneß lamented their finishing, and they have about two and a half days to recover; Angelo Stiller and Luca Jaquez are back and only Justin Diehl is out, as the numbers assume. Frankfurt had no midweek game and come off three home wins in a row, but Can Uzun is doubtful again: two reports (hessenschau, LigaInsider) say Adi Hütter has left his place open, and the numbers don't know that; Jessic Ngankam is out (counted). Sascha Stegemann referees (counted); no dedicated preview for this match was found, so the view rests on team news and form.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals, a high figure driven by Stuttgart's attack at home; the last two meetings here both ended 3-2. But Stuttgart have scored none in their last two games (Schalke, Inter), play on tired legs after Wednesday in Milan, and Frankfurt may be without Uzun, their main creator, which the numbers don't see. I lean a little lower, to about 3.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners and already lift Frankfurt for their 35 corners in the last six, and Stuttgart for conceding 42. Stuttgart's wide players (Leweling, Führich, Mittelstädt) are all available, and Hütter's talk of a back three with Doan as wing-back would keep Frankfurt's width, so I stay at 10.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards and already add for both teams' busier recent bookings and for Stegemann's slightly above-average record (4.1 a game). Hütter wants more pressing and intensity, but this is a race for Europe rather than a grudge match, so I stay at about 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.2 shots and already raise Frankfurt by about 20% because Stuttgart allowed 117 shots in their last six, much of that while Stiller was out. With Stiller and Jaquez back, Stuttgart tired after Inter, and Uzun doubtful for Frankfurt, I trim slightly to about 29.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.9 shots on target, already lifting Frankfurt 10% for their recent accuracy and trimming Stuttgart for poor finishing. Stuttgart managed one on target at Inter and look short of sharpness, and Uzun may miss out for Frankfurt, so I take a little off, to about 10.7.
